title: A Deadline for the Contact
premise: Rafael Dunmore's carefully compartmentalized life shatters when a real-estate listing for her off-books safe house appears online, its interior photos revealing the face of Marek Voss, a defector her agency was never supposed to know existed. Tasked with extracting Voss before a border checkpoint rotation exposes him, Rafael discovers he isn't a prize asset — he's bait, dangled by her own employer to flush out a mole inside the firm. As hunters close in and her crew becomes the only family she's ever trusted, Rafael must choose between delivering the lie that keeps her alive and burning her handlers to save the people she loves. She torches the contract, exposes the mole at a brutal checkpoint standoff, and walks away with Voss and her crew — alive, unemployed, and finally honest with each other.
about_author: Hazel Zhou is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction, and her thrillers are known for procedural precision and characters who lie beautifully. She lives in a coastal city she refuses to name, citing operational security.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Scrolling listings at 3 a.m., she finds her safe house for sale — every room photographed, including the panic room and a stranger's face in a hallway mirror. Her handler dismisses it as a glitch. The beat is cold dread: her polished lie has been published for anyone to bid on.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Her employer, Meridian Protective Group, assigns her to guard Marek Voss, a mid-level defector with a mediocre file — too mediocre. She recognizes the safe house in his debrief photos and realizes the listing was a message. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Crew
chapters.summary: Alternate POVs: ex-medic Suri, comms whiz Dev, and driver Okafor each get a scene showing why they've stayed with Rafael — debts, loyalty, nowhere else. She tells them nothing about the listing. Beat: found family warming against a gathering storm.

chapters.title: Bait in the File
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Digging into Voss's file, she finds the defector's intel is stale, his escape route suspiciously clean, and his extraction scheduled exactly at the checkpoint shift change. He isn't fleeing to them; he's being delivered. Beat: the sick click of understanding.

chapters.title: House Hunting
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Under guard, Voss reveals he recognized Rafael from surveillance photos in the listing — he knows she knows, and he's been ordered to keep her close. He offers her the truth about Meridian's mole in exchange for getting him out alive. Beat: two liars negotiating trust.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev maps the checkpoint rotations and finds the shift change isn't a window — it's a kill box, scheduled by someone with internal access. The mole is inside Meridian, and the extraction plan is the trap. Beat: the crew realizes they're the expendable variable.

chapters.title: What the Go-Bag Holds
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Meridian orders her to proceed as planned; refusal means her cover, her records, her life unravel. She unpacks her go-bag — cash, burned passports, a gun with a history — and finally tells the crew everything. Beat: confession as commitment; the lie dies so the family can live.

chapters.title: The Long Approach
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A white-knuckle drive to the border, tailing a Meridian shadow team, Suri treating a wound Voss took in an ambush that felt staged to herd them. Beat: rising dread, the crew functioning as one organism under fire.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the shift change, the mole — Rafael's own handler — springs the trap, intending to kill Voss, the crew, and the evidence. Rafael turns the extraction protocol against Meridian, broadcasting the handler's voice and orders to the border guards. Beat: the climax, betrayal met with audacity.

chapters.title: Off Contract
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue weeks later. The handler is exposed; Meridian disavows everything, and Rafael is officially a ghost. Voss, alive and free, offers her a name and a debt. The crew, unpaid and unemployable, stays anyway. Beat: quiet resolution — survival's price paid, family chosen.
